exemplars.title: Non-existent product uuid on line item must not crash event group creation
exemplars.text: Non-existent product uuid on line item must not crash event group creation. Setup: Authenticated purchaser. The decoded product id does not exist, or exists but is not Product.active in this workspace.. Steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a line item whose product_uuid decodes to an id with no matching active Product. 2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx and NOT a 500. 3. Assert no partially-created EventGroup is left behind, since create_line_items runs inside the ActiveRecord::Base.transaction.. Expected: HTTP 4xx expected (422 with a numeric code). Risk being probed: get_details_for_event_group_line_items does products.find { ... } then dereferences product.id, so an unmatched product would raise NoMethodError on nil and surface as 500. Either way the transaction must roll back and leave zero event_groups rows.

exemplars.text: Negative and non-numeric quantities must not be silently coerced into a valid event. Setup: Authenticated purchaser; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} are active.. Steps: 1. POST /event_groups with two line items: one with quantity value -5 and one with quantity value 'ten'. 2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx, or if accepted, assert the stored quantities are never negative. 3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items and inspect the persisted quantity values.. Expected: No 5xx. Documented hazard: the helper uses quantity[:value].to_f, so 'ten'.to_f becomes 0.0 and silently flips is_rate_only to true, while -5 survives as -5.0. A negative or silently rate-only line item must be refused with a numeric error code rather than persisted.

plan.title: Negative and non-numeric quantities must not be silently coerced into a valid event

exemplars.title: Converting with an auction type that does not exist crashes instead of being refused
exemplars.text: Converting with an auction type that does not exist crashes instead of being refused. Setup: {{tradeId}} is the sandbox RFQ (published, window open, one KG line, no bids). Base conversion body with the safety backstop.. Steps: 1. Send the base conversion body with `configurations.auction_config = "serial_bidding"` to `POST /trade/move_to_auction`. 2. Read the status.. Expected: A clean 4xx naming the bad type. Today: `change_rfq_info` assigns the value to the enum, Rails 7.0 raises ArgumentError ("'serial_bidding' is not a valid auction_config"), which is not a CustomException, is re-raised and is not rescued → HTTP 500. The transaction rolls back; the sandbox RFQ is untouched.

The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab. The sandbox's bid window ends ~30 minutes in the future.. Steps: Ask for the Live list for a range from 1 Jan 2024 to 2100 (the backend clamps the end to now). `GET /event_groups?filters=%7B%22starting_from%22%3A1704067200%2C%22ending_at%22%3A4102444800%7D`. Expected: The sandbox (created inside the range) should still be listed. Today it is excluded: create_filter_params clamps ending_at to now and filter_on_date adds `trade_requests.closed_at <= now`, which no open stage satisfies.

plan.title: Picking a date range on the Live tab hides every event that is still running

exemplars.title: Re-publishing an already live event changes nothing
exemplars.text: Re-publishing an already live event changes nothing. Setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is already active with stage {{tradeId}} live and vendor {{vendorUuid}} invited.. Steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. Read GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience and note the participant count. 2. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the exact publish body the journey sent. 3. Read the audience and stages again.. Expected: HTTP 200. The event is not a draft, so update_event_group_data takes the 'publish a new stage' branch (event_group_controller_helper.rb:29-31); every listed stage is already non-draft and is skipped by `next unless tr.draft?` (update_service.rb:267). Audience count, stage count and stage statuses are unchanged.

plan.title: Re-publishing an already live event changes nothing

exemplars.title: A publish body with no status publishes nothing but answers 200
exemplars.text: A publish body with no status publishes nothing but answers 200. Setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached (not yet published).. Steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the publish body minus `status`. 2. Read the event back.. Expected: No branch of update_event_group_data matches (status is nil, line_items empty, config absent — event_group_controller_helper.rb:29-36), so nothing is written and the controller renders 200 with the unchanged event. Correct behaviour would be a 422 code 2 (Insufficient parameters); today the client is told 'OK' for a publish that did not happen — even the new title is dropped.

plan.title: A publish body with no status publishes nothing but answers 200

exemplars.title: An unknown status together with a config change crashes with a 500
exemplars.text: An unknown status together with a config change crashes with a 500. Setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} (any state).. Steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with status "banana" and config {show_under_open_events: true}. 2. Check the response shape.. Expected: Must be a 422 {code, message}. Today `config.present?` routes into UpdateService#execute (event_group_controller_helper.rb:33-34), which does `@event_group.status = @status` (update_service.rb:79); assigning 'banana' to the EventGroup enum (in_active/active/draft/withdrawn) raises ArgumentError, which no rescue_from catches, so the answer is an untyped 500.

exemplars.title: An invited vendor can call add-audience on the buyer's live stage
exemplars.text: An invited vendor can call add-audience on the buyer's live stage. Setup: Signed in as the invited vendor of stage {{tradeId}}; the stage's config has no is_user_allowed_to_modify_audience key (the default).. Steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. As the vendor, PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with audience_to_add_uuids: ["{{vendorUuid}}"]. 2. Check the response.. Expected: Must be refused (422 code 455). Today the policy is add_audience_live_auction? → allowed_to_view_event? = show? (read_record) && is_allowed_to_view? (trade_request_policy.rb:125-127, 222-224) — both true for an invited vendor — and is_audience_modification_allowed? returns true when the config key is absent (trade_request_model_helper.rb:936-941). A vendor can add (or, via remove_audience, remove) participants.

plan.title: An invited vendor can call add-audience on the buyer's live stage

exemplars.title: Two publishes at once: the lock answers 516 but the second update still runs and then 500s
exemplars.text: Two publishes at once: the lock answers 516 but the second update still runs and then 500s. Setup: A draft copy with its stage attached.. Steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. Fire two identical publish PATCHes to /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} within the same second. 2. Compare both responses and read the event and audience.. Expected: Expected: one 200 and one 422 code 516 'Transaction in Progress' with no second write. Today lock_transaction renders 516 but only `return`s from itself (event_groups_controller.rb:1513-1518), so update carries on, performs the publish/update a second time and then renders again → AbstractController::DoubleRenderError → 500. The after_action also deletes the lock the other request holds (…:1522-1526).

exemplars.title: A percent-encoded folder name skips the company check
exemplars.text: A percent-encoded folder name skips the company check. Setup: The run's own draft event with one RFQ round (QA vendor 1 in the audience). Publishing notifies QA vendor 1 only.. Steps: Publish (`PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` with the publish body) with `attachments: [{"url": "https://procol.s3.amazonaws.com/trade%5Ffiles/terms_and_conditions/QA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]`.. Expected: Should be refused like the plain spelling (EDGE-PUB-024): HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'. Today the literal test misses `trade%5Ffiles`, so the event publishes (200) and the reader decodes the key back to `trade_files/…`.

exemplars.title: A URL on a different host is signed as a Procol file
exemplars.text: A URL on a different host is signed as a Procol file. Setup: The run's own draft event with one RFQ round.. Steps: Publish with `attachments: [{"url": "https://files.example.com/trade_files/terms_and_conditions/QA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]`.. Expected: Should be refused: HTTP 422, code 101. Today it publishes (200); the check only inspects URLs containing `amazonaws.com/trade_files/`, and the reader signs the path regardless of host. The check should judge the path, not the host string.

exemplars.title: An encoded slash defeats the company-id pattern
exemplars.text: An encoded slash defeats the company-id pattern. Setup: The run's own draft event with one RFQ round.. Steps: Publish with `attachments: [{"url": "https://procol.s3.amazonaws.com/trade_files/terms_and_conditions%2FQA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]`.. Expected: Should be refused: HTTP 422, code 101. Today the `/trade_files/<folder>/<name>_<id>/` pattern does not match when the slash is encoded, a non-match is allowed, and the event publishes (200); the signer later decodes `%2F`.

exemplars.text: A surrogate reference note with an outside-host file leaves a saved bid behind a server error. Setup: As EVD2-DOC-061; the company allows surrogate bids.. Steps: Enter a surrogate bid for QA vendor 1 with `surrogate_remarks: {remarks: "QA_Platform_ref_{{stamp}}", attachments: ["https://files.example.com/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"]}`.. Expected: Should be refused with 422 code 472 and no bid saved. Today the bid is saved, the remark fails validation, the helper renders 472 and returns nil, and the caller proceeds with a nil bid → HTTP 500 with the bid already stored.

exemplars.title: The reports list for a draft event is empty with no body
exemplars.text: The reports list for a draft event is empty with no body. Setup: The run's own draft event (one line item, no rounds), read by its owner.. Steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.. Expected: HTTP 204 No Content with an empty body — the action returns before rendering when the event is a draft, so Rails answers "no content". Clients expecting `{data: []}` must cope with an empty body. Must not be a 500.

exemplars.title: A live event lists its stage reports
exemplars.text: A live event lists its stage reports. Setup: The run's own live RFQ event, no bids, read by its owner.. Steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.. Expected: HTTP 200 `{data: […]}` with, for the RFQ round, 'RFQ report' (auction_bids_comparison_report) and 'RFQ Counter Offer Report' (counter_offer_report_v2), each with the round uuid and item_type trade_request. No QCS-Purchase yet (needs a participating vendor) and no Approval Note (no selected proposal).

exemplars.title: The reports list is returned to an invited vendor
exemplars.text: The reports list is returned to an invited vendor. Setup: The run's own live RFQ event; QA vendor 1 invited and has bid. Read by QA vendor 1 (vendor app).. Steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.. Expected: HTTP 200 and the vendor receives the buyer's report menu for rounds it can see — 'RFQ report', 'RFQ Counter Offer Report' and, once a vendor participates, 'QCS-Purchase', plus 'Approval Note-Purch' once a proposal is selected. Whether each report then downloads for a vendor is decided elsewhere and must be checked manually.

exemplars.title: The reports list is refused for an uninvited vendor
exemplars.text: The reports list is refused for an uninvited vendor. Setup: The run's own live RFQ event with QA vendor 1 invited; read by QA vendor 2, who is NOT invited.. Steps: As QA vendor 2, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' — `show?` needs at least one round visible to the caller; a restricted round hides it from an uninvited vendor.

exemplars.title: The reports list still answers after a withdrawal
exemplars.text: The reports list still answers after a withdrawal. Setup: The run's own live RFQ event, withdrawn by the buyer in the arrange step.. Steps: 1. Withdraw the event with a remark. 2. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.. Expected: HTTP 200: a withdrawn event is not a draft, so the list is built; the withdrawn round still shows 'RFQ report' and 'RFQ Counter Offer Report' (stages are listed whatever their status).

exemplars.title: Moving a draft technical round's end past the pricing round's end does not break the server
exemplars.text: Moving a draft technical round's end past the pricing round's end does not break the server. Setup: A fresh draft event with a technical (RFP) round and a pricing (RFQ) round, not published.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with `{"increase_auction_time": <RFQ end + 3600>, "remarks": "QA_Platform_extend_{{stamp}}"}`.. Expected: The change is applied or refused cleanly (a 4xx with a message). Never a server error. Today: HTTP 500.

exemplars.text: Moving a draft technical round's end to before the pricing round's end does not break the server. Setup: A fresh draft event with an RFP round and an RFQ round.. Steps: 1. exemplars.title: A vendor regrets a line on its own draft bid
exemplars.text: A vendor regrets a line on its own draft bid. Setup: A live RFQ with QA vendor 1 invited; the vendor has opened a draft bid and priced nothing.. Steps: As QA vendor 1 (vendor app), `PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/line_items/{{lineItemUuid}}/regret_status` with `{"company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "trade_request_uuid": "{{tradeId}}", "action_type": "regret"}`.. Expected: Accepted. The reply echoes the bid and labels the line as regretted; nothing changes on the line for the buyer yet — the regret only lives in the draft until the vendor saves or submits. HTTP 200 with `bid_uuid` and `status: {"value": "regretted", "label": "REGRET"}`.

exemplars.title: Regretting the same line twice is harmless
exemplars.text: Regretting the same line twice is harmless. Setup: As 001, and the line has already been regretted once on this draft.. Steps: Send the 001 request a second time.. Expected: Accepted again; the draft still holds the line once, as regretted (the entry is keyed by the line id and simply rewritten). HTTP 200, status label "REGRET".

exemplars.title: Undoing a regret before submitting gives a normal bid
exemplars.text: Undoing a regret before submitting gives a normal bid. Setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted (helper H01).. Steps: 1. `PATCH …/regret_status` with `"action_type": "undo_regret"`. 2. Price the line. 3. Submit the bid. 4. As the buyer, read the round.. Expected: The undo is accepted (the draft entry is removed; the line was never written as regretted, so nothing else changes), the bid submits normally and the buyer sees one live bid. Undo answers HTTP 200 with `status: {"value": null, "label": null}`.

exemplars.title: "Undo" with nothing to undo is accepted and changes nothing
exemplars.text: "Undo" with nothing to undo is accepted and changes nothing. Setup: A fresh draft of QA vendor 1, nothing regretted.. Steps: `PATCH …/regret_status` with `"action_type": "undo_regret"`.. Expected: Accepted as a no-op: the delete finds nothing and the bid is saved unchanged. HTTP 200, status value null.

exemplars.title: A line regretted in the draft can still be priced
exemplars.text: A line regretted in the draft can still be priced. Setup: A live RFQ (one round, no technical stage), QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted.. Steps: Price the regretted line (`POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products`).. Expected: Accepted. The price check that refuses regretted lines (736) reads only the line's saved `participants`, which a draft regret has not touched yet, and it only runs when a technical round exists. The regret wins later, at submit (see 006). HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: Regretting the only line and submitting leaves the vendor with no live bid
exemplars.text: Regretting the only line and submitting leaves the vendor with no live bid. Setup: A live one-round RFQ with one line; QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted (step 1 of this case).. Steps: 1. Regret the line. 2. Price it. 3. Submit the bid. 4. As the buyer read the round and the event's participants (`GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience`).. Expected: The submit is accepted. Right after activating the bid the server writes "regretted" onto the line for this vendor, marks the draft entry "processed", drops the priced line and — because no line is left — turns the whole bid "revised". The buyer's round shows no live bid, while the participants list still counts the vendor under "bid placed" (it includes revised bids). Submit answers HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: Submitting a regret-only draft (no prices) in a one-round event
exemplars.text: Submitting a regret-only draft (no prices) in a one-round event. Setup: A live one-round RFQ; QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted and no price.. Steps: Submit the draft (`PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}` with `status: "active"`).. Expected: A clean answer: either refused because nothing is priced (e.g. 372 'Please quote prices for all the products.' on a lot-closing round) or accepted and the bid immediately turned "revised" (the empty bid has no line to keep). Never a 5xx.

exemplars.title: Regretting every line on a new draft withdraws an already-submitted bid
exemplars.text: Regretting every line on a new draft withdraws an already-submitted bid. Setup: A live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has a submitted bid; the round's `lock_quote_after_submission` is off and no price-change approval applies.. Steps: 1. Open a new draft (it starts with the live bid's lines). 2. Regret the only line. 3. Re-price at 95. 4. Submit. 5. As the buyer, read the round.. Expected: The submit is accepted as a revision: the old bid becomes "revised", the new one is activated and then, because its only line is regretted, also turned "revised". The vendor ends with no live bid. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: Undo after submitting is refused because the bid is no longer a draft
exemplars.text: Undo after submitting is refused because the bid is no longer a draft. Setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1 regretted the line, priced it and submitted (the bid is now revised).. Steps: `PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/line_items/{{lineItemUuid}}/regret_status` with `"action_type": "undo_regret"` on the submitted bid.. Expected: Refused: only draft bids are looked up. HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.

exemplars.title: One-round event: the vendor can quote again on a regretted line, but the line stays flagged
exemplars.text: One-round event: the vendor can quote again on a regretted line, but the line stays flagged. Setup: A live one-round RFQ; QA vendor 1 regretted, priced and submitted (bid revised, line regretted).. Steps: 1–3 as 006. 4. Place a fresh bid on the line (open, price, submit). 5. As the buyer read the round.. Expected: The new bid is accepted: in a one-round event neither the price check (736) nor the submit check (800) runs, and the new draft carries no regret. The buyer sees one live bid. The stale "regretted" flag is the defect: the line should no longer be marked regretted once the vendor quotes it.

exemplars.title: Two-round event: a submitted regret blocks quoting that line again
exemplars.text: Two-round event: a submitted regret blocks quoting that line again. Setup: A live RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 submitted its technical response, then in the RFQ regretted the line, priced and submitted (bid revised).. Steps: 1–3 as 006 in the RFQ. 4. Place a fresh bid on the same line.. Expected: The new draft opens, but pricing the line is refused. HTTP 422, code 736 'You have declined to provide this line item; therefore, you are not permitted to quote for it commercially'.

exemplars.title: Two-round event: a regret-only draft cannot be submitted
exemplars.text: Two-round event: a regret-only draft cannot be submitted. Setup: A live RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 submitted its technical response (no "Regret" answer), opened an RFQ draft and regretted the line, priced nothing.. Steps: Submit the draft.. Expected: Refused: the "every non-regretted line must be priced" check reads only the line's saved `participants` (still "participated" from the technical response), not the draft regret. HTTP 422, code 748 'Please enter bid for all line items that are not regretted in technical stage.'

exemplars.text: Regret after the bidding window has closed. Today 200 — no window check exists; product to decide whether it should be 33 'Order not active'. Never a 5xx.

exemplars.text: Regret on an event that has been superseded by a new version. Setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a draft; the buyer issues a new version (not published).. Steps: Regret on the draft of the old version.. Expected: Should match the bid routes (422 code 101). Today 200 (no `latest?` check); never a 5xx.

exemplars.title: A vendor's event-level decline reaches the buyer's participants list
exemplars.text: A vendor's event-level decline reaches the buyer's participants list. Setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `POST /user_intents` with `{"item_uuid": "{{eventGroupUuid}}", "item_type": "EventGroup", "intent_type": "trade_reject", "reason": ["QA_Platform_reason_{{stamp}}"], "remarks": "QA_Platform_decline_{{stamp}}"}`. 2. As the buyer, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience`.. Expected: The decline is saved and the vendor's row shows the reason and remark. HTTP 200 `{"success": true}`.

exemplars.title: A round-level decline never reaches that list
exemplars.text: A round-level decline never reaches that list. Setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `POST /user_intents` with `item_type: "TradeRequest"`, `item_uuid: "{{tradeId}}"`, `intent_type: "trade_reject"` and a reason. 2. As the buyer read `get_audience`.. Expected: 200, and the vendor's "reason" column stays empty. The two places should read the same answer.

exemplars.title: Declining counts as having answered the participation question
exemplars.text: Declining counts as having answered the participation question. Setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.. Steps: 1. Round-level decline as in 058. 2. As QA vendor 1, `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`.. Expected: The round says the vendor has answered. HTTP 200 and `user_intent_answered: true` (the field is left out when false).

exemplars.title: A declined vendor can still bid, and the buyer sees both answers at once
exemplars.text: A declined vendor can still bid, and the buyer sees both answers at once. Setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.. Steps: 1. Event-level decline as in 057. 2. Vendor places a full bid. 3. As the buyer read `get_audience`.. Expected: Both accepted; the vendor row keeps the decline text and the stage lists the vendor as bid placed. Either the bid should be refused or the decline cleared when the vendor bids.

exemplars.title: Declining and then accepting: the latest answer wins in the vendor's event view
exemplars.text: Declining and then accepting: the latest answer wins in the vendor's event view. Setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1 already declined at event level (helper H02).. Steps: 1. `POST /user_intents` with `{"item_uuid": "{{eventGroupUuid}}", "item_type": "EventGroup", "intent_type": "trade_accept"}`. 2. As the vendor, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`.. Expected: Accept saved (no reason needed); the event view shows the acceptance. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: The vendor's own event view shows its decline and remark
exemplars.text: The vendor's own event view shows its decline and remark. Setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.. Steps: 1. Event-level decline as in 057. 2. As the vendor, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`.. Expected: HTTP 200; `user_intent` carries the decline and the remark.

exemplars.title: Joining through "participate" after declining records an acceptance the buyer never sees
exemplars.text: Joining through "participate" after declining records an acceptance the buyer never sees. Setup: Buyer company setting `enable_open_tender_events` ON; a live event; QA vendor 1 mapped to the buyer and has declined at event level (H02).. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants`. 2. Vendor reads the event. 3. Buyer reads `get_audience`.. Expected: Step 1 HTTP 200 `{"success": true}`; step 2 shows `user_intent.intent_type` = "trade_accept"; step 3 still shows the decline text (the new row has no `company_id`). Should store the vendor's company.

exemplars.title: The buyer rejects a submitted bid while bidding is open
exemplars.text: The buyer rejects a submitted bid while bidding is open. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; `disable_reject_bid_in_bidding_time` is off on the round.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 1's bid with a reason, allowing re-bidding: `PATCH /bids/{{bidUuid}}/reject` with `{"rejection_remarks": "QA_Platform_reject_{{stamp}}", "allow_rebidding": true}`.. Expected: The bid is rejected and the reason is stored for the vendor. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: Rejecting without allowing re-bidding puts the vendor on the round's block list
exemplars.text: Rejecting without allowing re-bidding puts the vendor on the round's block list. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with `"allow_rebidding": false`. 2. Read the round back as the buyer (`GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`).. Expected: The round's settings now list QA vendor 1 as not allowed to re-bid. HTTP 200 on both calls.

exemplars.title: A vendor blocked from re-bidding cannot place a new bid
exemplars.text: A vendor blocked from re-bidding cannot place a new bid. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with `"allow_rebidding": false`. 2. As QA vendor 1, try to place a new bid (open, price, submit).. Expected: Step 2 is refused at the first call. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

exemplars.title: A vendor allowed to re-bid can quote again after the rejection
exemplars.text: A vendor allowed to re-bid can quote again after the rejection. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with `"allow_rebidding": true`. 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.. Expected: Step 2 is accepted — the rejected bid does not count as an existing quote. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: Sending 'allow re-bidding' as the text "false" does not block the vendor
exemplars.text: Sending 'allow re-bidding' as the text "false" does not block the vendor. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject with `"allow_rebidding": "false"` (text). 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.. Expected: Step 2 is accepted — the vendor was not blocked. Should be treated like false (suspected looseness); today HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: Leaving out the re-bidding choice allows re-bidding
exemplars.text: Leaving out the re-bidding choice allows re-bidding. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid without the `allow_rebidding` field. 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.. Expected: Step 2 is accepted. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: A rejection with no reason is accepted by the API
exemplars.text: A rejection with no reason is accepted by the API. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with only `{"allow_rebidding": true}` (no `rejection_remarks`).. Expected: Today the rejection is stored with an empty reason (HTTP 200). Should be refused like the dialog does (suspected gap: the Remark model has no presence rule).

exemplars.text: Rejecting the same bid twice is refused. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid. 2. Reject the same bid again.. Expected: Step 2 is refused because the bid is no longer active. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

exemplars.title: Rejecting a bid that does not exist
exemplars.text: Rejecting a bid that does not exist. Setup: A signed-in buyer.. Steps: 1. `PATCH /bids/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/reject` with a reason.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists'.

As QA vendor 1, open a bid (`POST /v1/bids`). 2. As the buyer, reject that draft.. Expected: Step 2 is refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

exemplars.title: A bid can be rejected after bidding has closed
exemplars.text: A bid can be rejected after bidding has closed. Setup: A fresh RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid and the bidding window plus extra closing time are over.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid.. Expected: Accepted. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: A bid on a withdrawn event cannot be rejected
exemplars.text: A bid on a withdrawn event cannot be rejected. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, withdraw the event with a remark. 2. Reject the vendor's bid.. Expected: Step 2 is refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

exemplars.title: A bid on a submitted award cannot be rejected
exemplars.text: A bid on a submitted award cannot be rejected. Setup: A fresh RFQ the QA vendor bid on, closed, and awarded to that vendor (award submitted).. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the awarded vendor's bid.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 785 'Can not reject a bid which is selected for proposal' (or code 101 if submitting the proposal already moved the bid out of the active state).

exemplars.title: Script, SQL-like text and emoji in the reason are stored safely
exemplars.text: Script, SQL-like text and emoji in the reason are stored safely. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. Reject with a reason containing `<script>`, `' OR 1=1 --`, Chinese text and an emoji.. Expected: No server error; tags are stripped on the way in.

exemplars.text: A very long reason does not crash the rejection. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. Reject with a 6,000-character reason.. Expected: No server error (stored, or refused cleanly).

exemplars.text: Rejecting one vendor's bid leaves the other vendor's bid active. Setup: A fresh live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2, each with a submitted bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 1's bid. 2. Reject QA vendor 2's bid.. Expected: Step 2 is accepted — vendor 2's bid was still active after step 1. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: Blocking one vendor does not block another
exemplars.text: Blocking one vendor does not block another. Setup: A fresh live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2, each with a submitted bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 2's bid without re-bidding. 2. As QA vendor 1, revise its bid.. Expected: Step 2 is accepted. HTTP 200.

exemplars.title: The second vendor is blocked as well when it is the one rejected
exemplars.text: The second vendor is blocked as well when it is the one rejected. Setup: A fresh live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2, each with a submitted bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 2's bid without re-bidding. 2. As QA vendor 2, try to bid again.. Expected: Step 2 is refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

exemplars.title: Rejecting during bidding is refused where the round disables it
exemplars.text: Rejecting during bidding is refused where the round disables it. As the buyer, reject the bid while bidding is open.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 686 'Bid rejection is disabled while bidding is in progress'.

Expected: Accepted; the reply is the bid with status rejected. HTTP 200.

exemplars.text: A rejection through the status endpoint never blocks re-bidding. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid through the status endpoint. 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.. Expected: Step 2 is accepted. HTTP 200.

exemplars.text: A status call without a status is refused. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.. Steps: 1. Send only a remark, no status.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.text: Changing the status of a bid that does not exist. Setup: A signed-in buyer.. Steps: 1. `PATCH /bids/update_bid_status/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with status rejected.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.

exemplars.text: The status endpoint refuses changes after the close, unlike the reject action. Setup: A fresh RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid and the window is over.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, set the bid's status to rejected.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active'.

exemplars.text: 'Remove bid' on a live round answers success but leaves the bid in place. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. Expected: Today step 1 answers HTTP 200 and step 2 is accepted — the bid was still active. Should either remove the bid or refuse (suspected defect: success reported for a change that never happened).

Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' (whether revoking is allowed on the round or not).

Reject the bid through the status endpoint. 2. Send `{"status": "active"}`. 3. Reject it with the reject action (only possible when active).. Expected: Steps 2 and 3 are accepted. HTTP 200.

exemplars.text: A vendor discards its own draft bid. Setup: A fresh live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a bid and does not submit it.. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. `PATCH /bids/delete_draft_bid/{{bidUuid}}` as QA vendor 1.. Expected: Accepted; the draft becomes inactive. HTTP 200.

exemplars.text: A submitted bid cannot be discarded as a draft. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, call the draft-discard on the submitted bid.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists' (only drafts are looked up).

exemplars.text: Discarding the same draft twice is refused. Setup: A fresh live RFQ.. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. Discard it. 3. Discard it again.. Expected: Step 3 is refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists'.

exemplars.text: A draft can still be discarded after the round closed. Setup: A fresh live RFQ with a two-minute window; QA vendor 1 opens a bid; the window then closes.. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. Wait for the close. 3. Discard the draft.. Expected: Accepted. HTTP 200.

exemplars.text: The rejected-bids list answers after a rejection. Setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid. 2. `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/rejected_bids`.. Expected: Step 2 answers HTTP 200 with the rejected bid under QA vendor 1 and its reason.

exemplars.title: A started round cannot be moved to a later window, and its clock is untouched
exemplars.text: A started round cannot be moved to a later window, and its clock is untouched. Setup: A fresh live RFQ whose bidding started when it was published (about 20 minutes open), QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.. Steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`. 2. Read the round back (`GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`).. Expected: The reschedule is refused and the round still starts in the past and ends at its original time. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.

exemplars.text: A reversed window on a started round is refused by the "already started" rule first. Setup: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.. Steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+7200}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+3600}}}`.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.

exemplars.text: Sending only a new start time is silently ignored. Setup: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.. Steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}}`. 2. Read the round back.. Expected: HTTP 200 and nothing changes — the round still starts in the past. Should be refused (422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters') so the caller knows nothing happened.

exemplars.text: Sending only a new end time does not extend the round. Setup: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, no bids.. Steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`. 2. Read the round back.. Expected: HTTP 200 but the end does not move. Should be refused (code 2) or applied.

exemplars.title: A started technical round cannot be rescheduled
exemplars.text: A started technical round cannot be rescheduled. Setup: A fresh live RFP+RFQ event; both rounds started at publish; QA vendor 1 invited to both.. Steps: `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.. Expected: Refused. The evaluator step that runs before the guard only acts when `forms` are sent, so it writes nothing. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.

Steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422 with code 4 'Request not found' once the round's status is closed (closed RFQ rounds are not editable), or code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!' if the close job has not flipped the status yet.

Expected: Refused (HTTP 422): code 769 'You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created.' where the company has rfx projects on (a requested/selected proposal restricts RFQ changes — misleading wording, see API-XMAT-035), otherwise code 4 'Request not found' (closed) or 258.

exemplars.title: After the end is pulled in, a vendor cannot bid
exemplars.text: After the end is pulled in, a vendor cannot bid. Setup: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids. `counter_offer_modification_enabled` is off on the round (otherwise a vendor may still open a draft during the extra closing time).. Steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"increase_auction_time": {{now+90}}, "remarks": "QA_Platform_shorten_{{stamp}}"}`. 2. Wait until that end has passed. 3. As QA vendor 1, place a bid (open, price, submit). 4. Read the round back.. Expected: Step 1 is accepted (should be refused — an extension to an earlier time is a shortening). Step 3 is refused at the first call: HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active'.

plan.title: After the end is pulled in, a vendor cannot bid

act.say: The buyer moves the bid end IN to 90 seconds from now (an 'extension' to an earlier time).
Wait until the new (earlier) bid end has passed.
QA vendor 1 tries to bid after the new end.

plan.dependsOnSetting: counter_offer_modification_enabled is OFF on the round (otherwise a vendor may still open a draft during the extra closing time)

exemplars.title: A draft opened before the end was pulled in cannot be priced after it
exemplars.text: A draft opened before the end was pulled in cannot be priced after it. Setup: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.. Steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a draft bid. 2. As the buyer, pull the end in to now + 90 s. 3. Wait until it has passed. 4. As QA vendor 1, price the line on the draft from step 1.. Expected: Step 4 is refused (HTTP 422): code 32 'Bid not found' once the end-of-bidding job has discarded drafts, otherwise code 33 'Order not active' (or 508 'Not allowed to bid on this product' where counter-offer modification is on and the round is in its extra closing time).

plan.title: A draft opened before the end was pulled in cannot be priced after it

act.say: QA vendor 1 opens a draft bid while bidding is open.
The buyer moves the bid end IN to 90 seconds from now (an 'extension' to an earlier time).
Wait until the new (earlier) bid end has passed.
QA vendor 1 tries to price its draft after the new end.

exemplars.text: A blank "weight on" is refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Same as the happy path (API-EVDWGT-013) with `"weightage_on": ""`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A round that does not exist answers "insufficient parameters", not "not found"
exemplars.text: A round that does not exist answers "insufficient parameters", not "not found". Setup: Signed-in buyer only (recipe `none`).. Steps: `PATCH /trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.. Expected: Refused before any policy check. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (a 404 or code 4 'Request not found' would be clearer).

exemplars.title: A garbled round id is refused the same way
exemplars.text: A garbled round id is refused the same way. Setup: Recipe `none`.. Steps: `PATCH /trade/WrongUuid1=/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: Weights cannot be added to a draft round through this action
exemplars.text: Weights cannot be added to a draft round through this action. Setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round (recipe `draft_rfq`).. Steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A withdrawn event's round cannot be weighted
exemplars.text: A withdrawn event's round cannot be weighted. Setup: `published_rfq`, then the event is withdrawn with a remark (arrange step `withdraw_event`; QA vendor 1 is the only invitee).. Steps: 1. Withdraw the event. 2. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.. Expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: Adding a lot weight for an invited vendor makes the round a weighted round
exemplars.text: Adding a lot weight for an invited vendor makes the round a weighted round. Setup: `published_rfq` (live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids, no weights).. Steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": {"qa_freight_adj": {"label": "QA_Platform_Freight_{{stamp}}", "input_type": "absolute", "data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": "100"}}}}}`. Then read the round.. Expected: Saved. The round now reads as weighted, weights are "lot", the weight list is the new key plus "weighted_total", and QA vendor 1's value is 100. HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'.

exemplars.title: The first weight save also locks vendors' quantities (allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding)
exemplars.text: The first weight save also locks vendors' quantities (allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding). Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: The happy-path save, then read the round.. Expected: HTTP 200; `trade_config.allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding` is true afterwards. Product confirmation needed that a weight save should change bidding rules; at minimum the screen should say so.

exemplars.title: Vendors are told which criteria they are weighted on
exemplars.text: Vendors are told which criteria they are weighted on. Setup: `published_rfq`; the happy-path save.. Steps: Save, then read the round as QA vendor 1.. Expected: The vendor's terms include a line naming "QA_Platform_Freight_…". Today the list also names the synthetic "Weighted Total" column ("depend on QA_Platform_Freight_…, Weighted Total along with the Gross Total") — cosmetic defect.

exemplars.title: Saving a new value for the same weight replaces the old one
exemplars.text: Saving a new value for the same weight replaces the old one. Setup: `published_rfq`; arrange: the happy-path save (value 100).. Steps: Save the same key for QA vendor 1 with `"250"`, then read the round.. Expected: HTTP 200; QA vendor 1's value is 250, not 350.

exemplars.title: Leaving a weight out of the next save removes it
exemplars.text: Leaving a weight out of the next save removes it. Setup: `published_rfq`; arrange: save two weights (qa_freight_adj and qa_quality_pen).. Steps: Save again with only qa_freight_adj; read the round.. Expected: HTTP 200; the weight list is qa_freight_adj + weighted_total only; qa_quality_pen is gone from the values (its rows are set in-active).

exemplars.title: Weights cannot be cleared back to an unweighted round
exemplars.text: Weights cannot be cleared back to an unweighted round. Setup: `published_rfq`; arrange: the happy-path save.. Steps: `PATCH …/edit_weight_parameters` with `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": {}}}`; read the round.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'; the round is still weighted with qa_freight_adj. (Product gap: no way to remove all weights.)

exemplars.title: Weights do not stop the vendor from bidding
exemplars.text: Weights do not stop the vendor from bidding. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: 1. Buyer saves the happy-path weight. 2. QA vendor 1 opens, prices and submits a bid. 3. Read the round.. Expected: Both succeed; the round is still weighted.

exemplars.title: A vendor's unsubmitted draft bid does not lock the weights
exemplars.text: A vendor's unsubmitted draft bid does not lock the weights. Setup: `published_rfq`; QA vendor 1 opens a draft bid but does not submit it.. Steps: Buyer saves the happy-path weight.. Expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'.

exemplars.title: "Weight on" must be lot or line_item
exemplars.text: "Weight on" must be lot or line_item. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"weightage_on": "vendor"`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A table with no weights is refused
exemplars.text: A table with no weights is refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot"}}`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: Each weight must be an object, not a bare number
exemplars.text: Each weight must be an object, not a bare number. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `"values": {"qa_freight_adj": "100"}`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A weight needs a name
exemplars.text: A weight needs a name. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"label": " "`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A name made only of HTML tags is stripped to nothing and refused
exemplars.text: A name made only of HTML tags is stripped to nothing and refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"label": ""`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: The weight type must be absolute or relative
exemplars.text: The weight type must be absolute or relative. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"input_type": "percentage"`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: The weight type is case-sensitive
exemplars.text: The weight type is case-sensitive. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"input_type": "Relative"`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A weight with no vendor values is refused
exemplars.text: A weight with no vendor values is refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body without `"data"`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A weight sent as a JSON number is refused (only text numbers pass)
exemplars.text: A weight sent as a JSON number is refused (only text numbers pass). Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": 100}` (number, not text).. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Should be accepted (`is_a?(Numeric)`).

exemplars.title: A missing (null) vendor value is refused
exemplars.text: A missing (null) vendor value is refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": null}`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A relative weight of exactly 100% is refused
exemplars.text: A relative weight of exactly 100% is refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"input_type": "relative"` and value `"100"`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A relative weight of exactly -100% is refused
exemplars.text: A relative weight of exactly -100% is refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Relative, value `"-100"`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A relative weight just inside the range is accepted
exemplars.text: A relative weight just inside the range is accepted. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Relative, value `"99.99"`; read the round.. Expected: HTTP 200; QA vendor 1's value reads 99.99.

exemplars.title: A negative absolute weight (a credit) is accepted
exemplars.text: A negative absolute weight (a credit) is accepted. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Absolute, value `"-250"`; read the round.. Expected: HTTP 200; value reads -250.

exemplars.title: A non-numeric absolute weight is stored as zero
exemplars.text: A non-numeric absolute weight is stored as zero. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Absolute, value `"abc"`.. Expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!' and the vendor's value is 0.0. Should be HTTP 422 code 2.

exemplars.title: Line-item weights must be given per line, not as one number per vendor
exemplars.text: Line-item weights must be given per line, not as one number per vendor. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `"weightage_on": "line_item"`, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": "100"}`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: A line value that is itself an object is refused
exemplars.text: A line value that is itself an object is refused. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Line mode, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": {"v": 1}}}`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: Relative weights do not have to add up to 100
exemplars.text: Relative weights do not have to add up to 100. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Two relative weights for QA vendor 1: qa_freight_adj "60" and qa_quality_pen "70".. Expected: HTTP 200; both stored.

exemplars.title: Two weights with the same name are accepted
exemplars.text: Two weights with the same name are accepted. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Two keys (qa_freight_adj, qa_quality_pen) both labelled "QA_Platform_Same_{{stamp}}".. Expected: HTTP 200. Should be refused like the screen does.

exemplars.title: A weight can be set for a vendor who is not invited to the round
exemplars.text: A weight can be set for a vendor who is not invited to the round. Setup: `published_rfq` (QA vendor 2 is NOT invited).. Steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"{{vendor2Uuid}}": "100"}`.. Expected: HTTP 200 and a weight row for QA vendor 2. Should be refused (vendor not in audience).

exemplars.title: A weight for a company that does not exist reports success but saves nothing
exemplars.text: A weight for a company that does not exist reports success but saves nothing. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": "100"}`.. Expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'; no weight row; round marked weighted. Should be 422.

exemplars.title: A line weight for a line that does not exist reports success but saves nothing
exemplars.text: A line weight for a line that does not exist reports success but saves nothing. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Line mode, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": "100"}}`.. Expected: HTTP 200; nothing stored; round now "line_item" weighted. Should be 422.

exemplars.title: weightages sent as text (or a number) is refused, not a crash
exemplars.text: weightages sent as text (or a number) is refused, not a crash. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `{"weightages": "QA_Platform_weights_{{stamp}}"}` (also try `{"weightages": 5}` by hand).. Expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today the code path at trade_controller.rb:1779 raises TypeError → HTTP 500.

exemplars.title: weightages sent as a list is refused, not a crash
exemplars.text: weightages sent as a list is refused, not a crash. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `{"weightages": ["lot"]}`.. Expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today `Array#[](:weightage_on)` raises TypeError → HTTP 500.

exemplars.title: weightages sent as true is refused cleanly
exemplars.text: weightages sent as true is refused cleanly. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `{"weightages": true}`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

exemplars.title: The weight list sent as text crashes the validator
exemplars.text: The weight list sent as text crashes the validator. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": "QA_Platform_text"}}`.. Expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today `String#each` → NoMethodError → HTTP 500.

exemplars.title: A weight's vendor values sent as text crash the validator
exemplars.text: A weight's vendor values sent as text crash the validator. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"data": "QA_Platform_text"`.. Expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today `String#each` → NoMethodError → HTTP 500.

exemplars.title: A weight list sent as key/value pairs passes validation, writes rows, then crashes
exemplars.text: A weight list sent as key/value pairs passes validation, writes rows, then crashes. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": [["qa_freight_adj", {"label": "QA_Platform_Freight_{{stamp}}", "input_type": "absolute", "data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": "100"}}]]}}`.. Expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2 with nothing written. Today (suspected): HTTP 500 (NoMethodError `keys` for Array) after the Weightage row is saved.

exemplars.title: A garbled line id in line mode crashes the save
exemplars.text: A garbled line id in line mode crashes the save. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Line mode, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": {"WrongUuid1=": "100"}}`.. Expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today (suspected): TypeError from the `item_id: Integer` signature → HTTP 500.

exemplars.title: A weight key containing "uuid" is mangled by the id decoder
exemplars.text: A weight key containing "uuid" is mangled by the id decoder. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with the key `qa_uuid_bonus` instead of `qa_freight_adj`.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. (The screen builds keys from the typed name, so a weight called "uuid bonus" can never be saved.)

exemplars.title: Script text in a weight name is stripped before it is stored
exemplars.text: Script text in a weight name is stripped before it is stored. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with `"label": "QA_Platform_<script>alert(1)</script>_{{stamp}}"`; read the round.. Expected: HTTP 200; the stored name is "QA_Platform_alert(1)_…" (tags removed).

exemplars.title: HTML in a weight KEY is stored raw
exemplars.text: HTML in a weight KEY is stored raw. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with the key `qa_`.. Expected: HTTP 200 and the key kept verbatim in `misc.weightage.key_attributes`. Should be refused (keys limited to letters, digits, underscore).

exemplars.title: A 400-digit weight becomes Infinity and the round still reads
exemplars.text: A 400-digit weight becomes Infinity and the round still reads. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Absolute value of 400 nines; read the round.. Expected: Should be refused as out of range. Today: HTTP 200 and the value reads "Infinity". The round read must stay 2xx.

exemplars.title: A weight named "weighted_total" collides with the synthetic total column
exemplars.text: A weight named "weighted_total" collides with the synthetic total column. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with the key `weighted_total`.. Expected: HTTP 200 and `weighted_total` twice in the key list. Should be refused as a reserved key.

exemplars.title: A weight named like a bid column ("price") still leaves the schema readable
exemplars.text: A weight named like a bid column ("price") still leaves the schema readable. Setup: `published_rfq`.. Steps: Happy-path body with the key `price`; read the buyer schema.. Expected: Should be refused (reserved widget key). Today: HTTP 200; the schema read must not crash.

exemplars.title: Once a vendor has bid, RFQ weights are locked unless the round allows edits
exemplars.text: Once a vendor has bid, RFQ weights are locked unless the round allows edits. Setup: Live RFQ with QA vendor 1's submitted bid (recipe `rfq_with_bid`); round `trade_config.allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` off/absent.. Steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with the happy-path body.. Expected: Refused, nothing changed. HTTP 422, code 15 'Operation failed' — the same generic code also means "not a rank round" (§6, 068), so the screen cannot say "bids already received".

exemplars.title: With allow_edit_weight_param_rfq on, weights can be added after bids
exemplars.text: With allow_edit_weight_param_rfq on, weights can be added after bids. Setup: `rfq_with_bid` on a company whose template sets `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` true.. Steps: Happy-path save.. Expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'.

exemplars.title: Weights can still be added after the bidding window closed with no bids
exemplars.text: Weights can still be added after the bidding window closed with no bids. Setup: RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids, window and extra time over (recipe `closed_rfq`).. Steps: Happy-path save.. Expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!' (or 422 code 2 if the round has already been moved to closed). Should be refused after close.

exemplars.title: A closed round with a bid refuses weight changes
exemplars.text: A closed round with a bid refuses weight changes. Setup: `closed_rfq_with_bid`; `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` off.. Steps: Happy-path save.. Expected: Refused: HTTP 422 code 15 'Operation failed' while the round is still active, or code 2 'Insufficient parameters' once it is closed.

exemplars.title: An awarded round refuses weight changes
exemplars.text: An awarded round refuses weight changes. Setup: `awarded_rfq` (bid in, closed, proposal submitted); `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` off.. Steps: Happy-path save.. Expected: Refused: 422 code 15 or code 2 (see 066). With the setting on and the round still active the API would accept — there is no award check.

exemplars.title: A technical (RFP) round cannot be weighted
exemplars.text: A technical (RFP) round cannot be weighted. Setup: Live RFP + RFQ event (recipe `published_rfp_rfq`).. Steps: `PATCH /trade/{{technicalTradeUuid}}/edit_weight_parameters` with the happy-path body.. Expected: HTTP 422, code 15 'Operation failed'.

exemplars.title: A vendor can read the weights set for a competitor
exemplars.text: A vendor can read the weights set for a competitor. Setup: `published_rfq`; the buyer saves weights for QA vendor 1 ("100") and QA vendor 2 ("300").. Steps: 1. Buyer saves. 2. QA vendor 1 reads the round (`GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`).. Expected: The vendor's read carries no value for QA vendor 2 (ideally no `weightages` at all). Today (suspected): `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<vendor 2>` = "300.0" is visible to vendor 1.
